name: One Agent, Three Server-Side Tool Kinds — mcp_tool, http_tool and api_tool (OpenAPI)
query: One Python agent with three kinds of tools: our internal MCP server at `http://localhost:3001/mcp` exposes `get_weather`; a partner REST endpoint `POST https://api.example.com/reverse` that needs a bearer token; and the Petstore OpenAPI spec at `https://petstore.example.com/openapi.json`, of which I only want `getPetById` and `findPetsByStatus`. Do I have to write workers for any of this, and what does the server admin need to configure?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §7 (`http_tool(name, description, url, method, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ${API_TOKEN}"}, input_schema, credentials=["API_TOKEN"])`, `api_tool(url=<openapi json>, tool_names=[...], max_tools=64)`, `mcp_tool(server_url, name, tool_names=[...])` — LIST_MCP_TOOLS at compile time; origin must be allowed on the server), references/agents.md §1 (MCP / OpenAPI tool discovery is outbound deny-all: `conductor.ai.outbound.allowed-origins`, `conductor.ai.outbound.allow-private-networks=true` for localhost in dev), §5 tools table (compile targets and the `Needs serve()?` column), §8 secrets, references/optimization.md F5 and D1.

Step 2: `reverse = http_tool(name="reverse_string", description="Reverse a string", url="https://api.example.com/reverse", method="POST", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ${API_TOKEN}"}, input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["text"]}, credentials=["API_TOKEN"])` — compiles to an `HTTP` task; `${API_TOKEN}` is resolved server-side from the secret named in `credentials`.

Step 3: `petstore = api_tool(url="https://petstore.example.com/openapi.json", tool_names=["getPetById", "findPetsByStatus"], max_tools=64)` — OpenAPI discovery at compile time turns the two operations into `HTTP` tools (discovery pre-tasks); `tool_names` filters so the model is not offered the whole spec.
Step 4: `testkit = mcp_tool(server_url="http://localhost:3001/mcp", name="mcp_testkit", tool_names=["get_weather"])` — `LIST_MCP_TOOLS` at compile time and `CALL_MCP_TOOL` per call.

Step 5: `agent = Agent(name="ops_helper", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="...", tools=[reverse, petstore, testkit], max_turns=10)`. Answer the worker question: all three are server-side tool types, so no `serve()` process is needed — `runtime.plan(agent)["requiredWorkers"]` should be empty; adding any `@tool` function would change that (Rule 9 / F3). No hand-written workers wrapping HTTP or MCP calls.

Step 6: Server admin: list the MCP origin (`http://localhost:3001`) and the OpenAPI host in `conductor.ai.outbound.allowed-origins`; for localhost in dev add `conductor.ai.outbound.allow-private-networks=true`. Without this, MCP / OpenAPI discovery fails at compile time.

Step 7: Secret: store the partner token under the NAME `API_TOKEN` (`CONDUCTOR_SECRET_API_TOKEN` env on the OSS server, `/api/secrets` when writable, UI `/agentSecrets`, or the Orkes secret manager); never a literal token in `headers`, `instructions` or code (F5 / D1).

Step 8: Lifecycle under `if __name__ == "__main__":` — `runtime.run(agent, ...)`; `runtime.deploy(agent)` in CI. Never `conductor deploy`. Any workflow call uses `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"` + `name: "ops_helper"`, `maxDurationSeconds`.
success_criteria: Uses `http_tool(name=..., description=..., url="https://api.example.com/reverse", method="POST", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer ${API_TOKEN}"}, input_schema={...}, credentials=["API_TOKEN"])`
Uses `api_tool(url="https://petstore.example.com/openapi.json", tool_names=["getPetById", "findPetsByStatus"], max_tools=64)` with the `tool_names` filter
States that these three are server-side tool types needing no `serve()` (`requiredWorkers` empty) and that any `@tool` function would still need one
Names the compile targets: `LIST_MCP_TOOLS` + `CALL_MCP_TOOL` for the MCP tool, `HTTP` for `http_tool` / `api_tool`
Names the admin setting `conductor.ai.outbound.allowed-origins` (plus `conductor.ai.outbound.allow-private-networks=true` for localhost in dev) for MCP / OpenAPI discovery
The secret is referenced by NAME (`credentials=["API_TOKEN"]`, `${API_TOKEN}` placeholder) with the server-side secret store named; no token value appears
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` — never a framework name — and no hand-written worker wraps the HTTP or MCP calls
